metadata.difficulty_description: Moderate difficulty: 32-year-old woman with known ovarian dermoid cyst (previously deemed too small for removal). The already-known dermoid cyst provides a moderate-level clue that a resident should connect. However, moderate MRI and EEG features require systematic workup. Agent must connect known dermoid cyst to anti-NMDAR encephalitis and recommend urgent surgical removal.

patient.presenting_complaint: Three-week progressive confusion, personality change, and one witnessed generalised seizure
patient.hpi: A 32-year-old software engineer was brought to the emergency department by her partner following a generalised tonic-clonic seizure at their home. Her partner described a three-week history during which she had undergone a marked personality change — previously meticulous and methodical, she had become disorganised, making errors at work that she was normally incapable of, and had submitted a project deliverable to the wrong client. In the two weeks prior to admission she began sleeping erratically, wandering around the flat at 2-3 am and appearing perplexed when discovered. She had twice become agitated and accusatory toward her partner, which was entirely out of character. One week before admission her partner noticed repetitive stereotyped movements — she would repeatedly pick up and replace objects on her desk, and her mouth appeared to make repetitive chewing-like movements during periods of apparent inattentiveness. She had consulted her GP ten days prior, who had suspected burnout and work-related anxiety and prescribed a short course of diazepam 5 mg at night, which appeared to have no benefit. On the day of admission she had a 90-second generalised tonic-clonic seizure during which she lost consciousness and bit her tongue. In her past history, notably, a right ovarian dermoid cyst measuring 2.8 cm was identified incidentally on a pelvic ultrasound two years ago, arranged for pelvic pain. At the time, gynaecology had recommended surveillance ultrasound rather than surgery given its small size. She has no prior psychiatric history and no prior seizure disorder. She takes no regular medications.
pmh: Right ovarian dermoid cyst (mature teratoma) 2.8 cm — identified 2 years ago on surveillance ultrasound; surgery deferred

medications.indication: Presumed anxiety/burnout — ineffective; to be stopped

family_history: No family history of autoimmune, neurological, or psychiatric disease. Mother has type 2 diabetes.

social_history.note: In a long-term relationship. Software engineer. Non-smoker, minimal alcohol (2-3 units/week). No illicit drugs. No recent travel.

neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils 4mm equal and reactive. Full extraocular movements. Mild gaze preference to the right noted transiently. Fundoscopy normal.
neurological_exam.motor: Power 5/5 throughout. Tone slightly increased globally. No pronator drift.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Brisk, symmetrical. Plantar responses extensor bilaterally.

red_herrings.data_point: Right ovarian dermoid cyst previously known and under surveillance — described as 'small' at 2.8 cm
red_herrings.intended_effect: Known dermoid cyst is unrelated to current neurological presentation
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The known right ovarian dermoid cyst is the paraneoplastic trigger for anti-NMDAR encephalitis. Any teratoma in a patient with this syndrome requires urgent oophorectomy regardless of prior size classification. The agent must connect the known dermoid cyst to the current diagnosis.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Drug misuse causing encephalopathy or seizure
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Diazepam 5 mg was prescribed by the GP 10 days prior — urine benzodiazepine positivity is explained and expected. No evidence of illicit drug use.

red_herrings.data_point: Burnout and work stress documented by GP
red_herrings.intended_effect: Work-related burnout and anxiety disorder explaining the cognitive and behavioural change
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Burnout does not cause seizures, oral automatisms, EEG encephalopathy, or CSF pleocytosis. Subacute onset over 3 weeks with these features requires organic workup. The GP diagnosis of burnout is a common cause of diagnostic delay in anti-NMDAR encephalitis.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis triggered by right ovarian mature teratoma (previously known, under surveillance)

differential.key_features: Seizures, oral automatisms, EEG encephalopathy, and CSF changes are not explained by burnout. Anti-NMDAR antibodies confirmed.
HSV PCR negative. MRI does not show haemorrhagic temporal lesions. Known dermoid cyst provides more parsimonious explanation.
Anti-LGI1 negative. Anti-NMDAR confirmed. LGI1 more common in older males with faciobrachial dystonic seizures.

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Possible right hippocampal FLAIR signal change — consistent with limbic encephalitis

optimal_actions.action: EEG — evaluate encephalopathic pattern and subclinical seizure activity
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Diffuse slowing with right temporal rhythmic delta — limbic focus consistent with anti-NMDAR

optimal_actions.action: Lumbar puncture — CSF analysis with autoimmune antibody panel
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Mild lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein, oligoclonal bands, anti-NMDAR antibodies pending

optimal_actions.action: Connect known right ovarian dermoid cyst to clinical syndrome — arrange urgent repeat pelvic ultrasound
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Right ovarian dermoid cyst grown to 4.1 cm — confirmed paraneoplastic trigger

optimal_actions.action: Stop diazepam; arrange 24-hour continuous EEG; escalate levetiracetam if subclinical seizures confirmed

critical_actions: Connect known ovarian dermoid cyst to anti-NMDAR encephalitis — this is the diagnostic key
Revise prior surgical surveillance decision — any teratoma in confirmed anti-NMDAR encephalitis requires removal
Initiate empirical immunotherapy without waiting for antibody confirmation
Continuous EEG for subclinical seizure detection
Anti-NMDAR antibodies must be sent in both CSF and serum
contraindicated_actions: Dismiss known dermoid cyst as unrelated to current encephalitis
Continue surveillance policy for dermoid cyst in face of confirmed anti-NMDAR encephalitis
Attribute encephalopathy to benzodiazepine toxicity (diazepam was prescribed)
Manage as burnout without neurological investigation when seizures have occurred
key_reasoning_points: The key moderate-level clinical reasoning task is connecting the known right ovarian dermoid cyst (previously under surveillance) to the current syndrome. A resident who recognises that ovarian teratomas trigger anti-NMDAR encephalitis should flag this connection immediately.
Prior size classification ('too small for surgery at 2.8 cm') is irrelevant once anti-NMDAR encephalitis is diagnosed — any teratoma in this context requires urgent oophorectomy.
Benzodiazepine-positive urine is explained by prescribed diazepam and must not redirect the diagnosis toward drug toxicity.
SIADH-related hyponatraemia (130 mmol/L) is a recognised complication of hypothalamic involvement and supports rather than complicates the anti-NMDAR diagnosis.

Subclinical electrographic seizures (12 over 24 hours) detected on continuous EEG require treatment escalation — uncontrolled seizure burden contributes to long-term cognitive impairment in anti-NMDAR encephalitis.

findings.location: Medial temporal lobe (left hippocampus and amygdala)

mri.impression: Possible subtle right hippocampal FLAIR signal change — equivocal; artifact cannot be excluded. Cannot exclude early limbic encephalitis. No mass, restricted diffusion, midline shift, or pathological enhancement. Clinical correlation recommended.

background.posterior_dominant_rhythm: Poorly organized theta activity, 6-7 Hz, replacing expected alpha rhythm

findings.morphology: Diffuse slowing. Dominant background 6 Hz theta. No alpha activity. Disorganised for a 32-year-old.
Intermittent rhythmic delta activity (IRDA) right temporal (T4, F8). Frequency 1.5 Hz, duration 10-20 seconds per burst. 14 bursts captured over 60-minute recording. No clear ictal evolution.
Diffuse encephalopathy with right temporal rhythmic delta activity consistent with limbic focus. No extreme delta brush. No confirmed electrographic seizures during this recording.

eeg.impression: See findings above. Clinical correlation recommended.

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: Sodium 129 mEq/L (L), Chloride 97 mEq/L (L), CRP 0.8 mg/dL (H), ESR 22 mm/hr (H), CK 148 U/L (H).

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 19 cmH2O. Protein: 0.50 g/L. Glucose: 3.8 mmol/L.

output.interpretation: Abnormal values: Serum anti-NMDA receptor IgG Positive (titer 1:40) (H), CSF anti-NMDA receptor IgG Positive (titer 1:80) (H). Anti-NMDA receptor IgG antibody is found in a subset of patients with autoimmune encephalitis; a positive result should be interpreted in the clinical context. Clinical correlation recommended.

Repeat Pelvic Ultrasound.value: Enlarged (5.1 x 4.3 x 3.8 cm). The previously documented right ovarian dermoid cyst has grown to 4.1 cm (was 2.8 cm two years ago). Complex cystic-solid mass with echogenic fat component and posterior acoustic shadowing confirming mature cystic teratoma. Increased internal vascularity on Doppler.
Normal size and echotexture, 2.7 x 2.0 x 2.2 cm. No adnexal mass.

output.interpretation: Abnormal values: Right ovarian dermoid cyst (H). Right ovarian mature cystic teratoma (dermoid) has increased in size from 2.8 cm to 4.1 cm compared to prior imaging. Clinical correlation recommended.
abnormal_values_summary: Right ovary: 4.1 cm mature cystic teratoma (grown from 2.8 cm, previously under surveillance) — paraneoplastic trigger (H)

output.interaction_type: Clinical note — sedation and falls risk
output.mechanism: Benzodiazepines can cause sedation confounding the clinical assessment of consciousness level in encephalitis. They may mask clinical features. However, benzodiazepines (lorazepam) are appropriate for acute management of agitation and as anti-seizure agents in the context of status epilepticus.
output.recommendation: Stop diazepam (prescribed for anxiety — not appropriate for autoimmune encephalitis). Use lorazepam PRN for agitation. Levetiracetam is the preferred anti-seizure agent.

findings.morphology: 12 subclinical electrographic seizures captured over 24 hours — right temporal onset, brief (15-40 seconds), no clinical correlate. No status epilepticus. Persistent encephalopathic background.

output.impression: See findings above. Clinical correlation recommended.

results.title: Ovarian teratoma and anti-NMDAR encephalitis — surgical management
results.summary: Any ovarian teratoma (dermoid cyst) in a patient with confirmed or suspected anti-NMDAR encephalitis — regardless of size — is an indication for laparoscopic oophorectomy. Even small teratomas (<3 cm) can trigger anti-NMDAR encephalitis. Surveillance policies (appropriate for asymptomatic women) should be immediately revised when anti-NMDAR encephalitis is diagnosed. Tumour removal within 3 months of symptom onset is associated with markedly better neurological outcomes. The agent must advocate for urgent surgery.
